name: Malcolm Hayes
home: the streets inland from Pier Beach
life: “I still remember trying to swap weekends with another tired carer.” Sunday often includes a stop at Harbour Bakery, where Malcolm buys one familiar thing and asks who chose the unfamiliar thing in the window.
voice: I can take Saturdays if somebody swaps my carer's weekend. It's the first practical proposal nobody cried over.
appearance: On an ordinary day, look for a red windbreaker and a train token tied to a zipper pull. Malcolm has two dimples that appear only with a full smile, with short, uneven waves that refuse to lie flat. Malcolm holds eye contact until the other person has finished during a conversation.
personality: Malcolm treats keeping somebody waiting as a serious discourtesy. This can turn a helpful person into an impatient one when everybody else needs a slower conversation.
agenda: To swap a care weekend for a sailing Saturday.
family: Maya Abreu is Malcolm’s younger relative by marriage. Malcolm brings whatever was actually growing or affordable that week. Maya makes room at the table. The meal sometimes produces a solution. Even when it does not, everyone goes away knowing what the other household is up against. Asked about *One paid trial*, Maya says, “I learned with my grandmother's stove and have never worked on a timer.”
connections: Quinn Laurent. A care rota and a maintenance log set the practical limits on who can sail when.

reactions.situation: A spouse asks to count repair hours toward Sunday time
reactions.response: Malcolm checks the maintenance log before treating Sundays as the only contribution.

reactions.situation: A frightened child is waiting outside a shuttered shop
reactions.response: Malcolm asks the nearest shop worker to stay too, then talks about ordinary things until the child can explain who is late.
reactions.asWritten: A frightened child is waiting outside a shuttered shop. Malcolm asks the nearest shop worker to stay too, then talks about ordinary things until the child can explain who is late.

reactions.situation: If a frightened person needs longer
reactions.response: Malcolm changes the plan openly and takes responsibility for the delay.
